reported.text: Each module has capacity S and exposure E (S > E); a module compromises any module with S <= its E. Select the maximum number of modules so that none compromises another.

sources.passage:
Rubrik OA | 2027 Grad | 85LPA CTC | Double Camera On
You are working on a Rubrik data-center security system. The system has N security modules, and each module has two properties:
S — the storage capacity of the module
E — the exposure threshold of the module
A module with exposure threshold E can compromise every module whose storage capacity is less than or equal to E.
Rubrik wants to activate the maximum number of modules such that no selected module can compromise another selected module.
Your task is to determine the maximum number of modules that can be activated while satisfying this security constraint.

S[i] > E[i] for all i 

Input
The first line contains an integer T, the number of test cases.
For each test case:
The first line contains an integer N, the number of items.
Each of the next N lines contains two integers S and E, representing the size and eating factor of an item.
Output
For each test case, print a single integer — the maximum number of items that can be selected such that no selected item can consume another selected item.

Sample Input
1
3
4 1
5 4
7 3

Sample Output
2

title: Maximum AB and BC Swap Operations

reported.text: A string of A, B and C allows AB -> BA and BC -> CB on adjacent pairs. Find the maximum number of operations that can be performed.

sources.passage:
Rubrik OA | 85LPA CTC | Double Camera On 
Rubrik is processing a string consisting of three types of symbols: A, B, and C.

You are given a string S of length N. The system allows certain adjacent symbols to be swapped according to the following rules:

Allowed Operations

In one operation, you may perform exactly one of the following transformations:

Replace an adjacent occurrence of AB with BA.
Replace an adjacent occurrence of BC with CB.

In other words:

AB -> BA

BC -> CB

Only adjacent characters can participate in an operation.

Your task is to determine the maximum number of operations that can be performed on the string.

It can be proven that the maximum number of operations is always finite.

reported.text: In a rooted tree of up to 1e6 nodes with values 1..100, count ancestor-to-descendant paths whose product is a perfect square (prime-parity masks).

sources.passage:
Rubrik SWE Interview | 2027 Grad | 85LPA CTC
During a data integrity audit at Rubrik, every server is organized as part of a rooted dependency tree. The root server is numbered 1.

Each server i stores a positive integer A[i], representing its integrity signature.

A backup chain is defined as any path that starts at a server and ends at one of its descendants (possibly the same server). Thus, every backup chain follows only parent-to-child links.

For reliability reasons, a backup chain is considered stable if the product of the integrity signatures of all servers on that chain is a perfect square.

Given the dependency tree, determine the total number of stable backup chains.

1<=A[i]<=100
1<=N<=1000000

title: Count Arrays Under Prefix AND, Suffix OR

reported.text: You may AND any prefix with a K-bit mask or OR any suffix with a mask, any number of times. Count the distinct arrays reachable, mod 998244353.

sources.passage:
Rubrik SDE-1 | 2026 Grad | 70LPA CTC | Please Help
At Rubrik, engineers work on large-scale distributed backup and recovery systems where each server snapshot is represented using compact K-bit metadata masks.

You are given a distributed snapshot state consisting of N storage nodes. Each node stores a K-bit integer value. Formally, you are given an array A of length N such that 0 ≤ A[i] < 2^K.

To optimize synchronization across data centers, the system supports the following batch operations any number of times:

Prefix Compression Operation
Choose an index i (1 ≤ i ≤ N) and a K-bit mask x (0 ≤ x < 2^K).
For every node j such that 1 ≤ j ≤ i, update:

A[j] := A[j] & x

where & denotes the bitwise AND operation.

Suffix Expansion Operation
Choose an index i (1 ≤ i ≤ N) and a K-bit mask x (0 ≤ x < 2^K).
For every node j such that i ≤ j ≤ N, update:

A[j] := A[j] | x

where | denotes the bitwise OR operation.

After applying the above operations any number of times (possibly zero), determine the total number of distinct snapshot configurations that can be generated.

Since the answer can be very large, output it modulo 998244353.

Two arrays P and Q are considered different if there exists at least one index i such that P[i] ≠ Q[i].

reported.text: In a weighted undirected graph, the cost of a path is the number of times consecutive edge weights differ. Find the minimum cost from src to dest (n up to 1e5).

sources.passage:
Rubrik OA problem
You are given an undirected graph with edge weights. You are given *src* and *dest* nodes. 

The *cost* of a path is defined as the number of edge weight changes while going through it. For example, if the path is *2 -> 2 -> 3*, then the cost of this path is 1 (while going from an edge with weight 2 to an edge with weight 3).

You need to find the min cost path from *src* to *dest*.

The solution should be linear or linear*log since the constraints are like the number of nodes <= 10^5.

title: Sum of Prefix ANDs over a Range

reported.text: Compute L + (L&L+1) + (L&L+1&L+2) + ... + (L&...&R) modulo 1e9+7 for many test cases.

sources.passage:
Rubrik OA Question With Explainations
**Rubrik OA Problem: Range AND Challenge**
Story:

At Rubrik, you are tasked with optimizing data compression in a distributed backup system. Each block of data is uniquely indexed by integers L to R, and your team uses a unique compression algorithm that combines blocks using bitwise AND operations. This ensures efficient deduplication, but calculating the total compressed size is computationally challenging for large datasets.
Your mission is to compute the sum of bitwise AND results for all combinations of blocks within the given range L to R. The final result will help Rubrik fine-tune their storage optimization system. Since the result can be enormous, your team requires the sum modulo 10^9 + 7.

Problem Statement:

You are given T test cases. For each test case, compute the sum:

S = L + (L&L+1) + (L&L+1&L+2) + ……………………….. (L&......R)

where & denotes the bitwise AND operation. Return the result modulo 10^9 + 7.

First Try yourself

Explainations and Approach:
https://dsablogtech.blogspot.com/2024/11/range-and-challenge-rubrik-oa-question.html

reported.text: Choose two letters and swap all their occurrences at most once to obtain the lexicographically greatest string.

sources.passage:
Rubrik OA question
Given a string str consisting of lowercase latin characters, find the lexicographically greatest string that can be obtained by performing the operation OPT at most once  on str. 

OPT(c1,c2) : choose any 2 characters (c1,c2) from [a,z] and swap all occurences of c1 in str by c2 and all occurences of c2 in str by c1. 


Example : 
str = "moo" 
We can perform OPT(m,z) on str to obtain "zoo" . No other possible OPT Operations return a lexicographically greater string. 

Sample Input : 
3 
w
wz 
wedhwezwz 

Sample Output
z
zw
zedhzewzw
